concepts.name: Table 4.1 (part 1): Parts I to X of the Constitution
concepts.description: Subjects and Articles covered by Parts I to X.
concepts.idea: Parts I to X cover the Union, citizenship, rights, directives, Union and State governments, territories and local bodies.
concepts.rule: Part I: The Union and its territory (Articles 1-4). Part II: Citizenship (5-11). Part III: Fundamental Rights (12-35). Part IV: Directive Principles (36-51). Part IV-A: Fundamental Duties (51A). Part V: The Union Government (52-151) with chapters: Executive (52-78), Parliament (79-122), Legislative Powers of the President (123), Union Judiciary (124-147), CAG (148-151). Part VI: State Governments (152-237): General (152), Executive (153-167), State Legislature (168-212), Legislative Powers of Governor (213), High Courts (214-232), Subordinate Courts (233-237). Part VII (Part B states, Article 238) was deleted. Part VIII: Union Territories (239-242). Part IX: Panchayats (243-243O). Part IX-A: Municipalities (243P-243ZG). Part IX-B: Co-operative Societies (243ZH-243ZT). Part X: Scheduled and Tribal Areas (244-244A).
concepts.example: Part IV-A has only one Article, 51A.

concepts.name: Table 4.1 (part 2): Parts XI to XXII of the Constitution
concepts.description: Subjects and Articles covered by Parts XI to XXII.
concepts.idea: Parts XI to XXII cover Centre-State relations, finance, services, elections, languages, emergency and amendment.
concepts.rule: Part XI: Relations between the Union and the States (245-263): legislative relations (245-255) and administrative relations (256-263). Part XII: Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits (264-300A): Finance (264-291), Borrowing (292-293), Property, contracts, rights, liabilities, obligations and suits (294-300), Right to Property (300A). Part XIII: Trade, Commerce and Intercourse (301-307). Part XIV: Services under the Union and States (308-323): Services (308-314), Public Service Commissions (315-323). Part XIV-A: Tribunals (323A-323B). Part XV: Elections (324-329A). Part XVI: Special Provisions relating to Certain Classes (330-342A). Part XVII: Official Language (343-351): Language of the Union (343-344), Regional Languages (345-347), Language of Courts (348-349), Special Directives (350-351). Part XVIII: Emergency Provisions (352-360). Part XIX: Miscellaneous (361-367). Part XX: Amendment (368). Part XXI: Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions (369-392). Part XXII: Short title, commencement, Hindi text and repeals (393-395). Part IV-A and XIV-A were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976), Part IX-A by the 74th (1992) and IX-B by the 97th (2011).

concepts.name: Table 4.3: the twelve Schedules
concepts.description: The subject matter of the First to Twelfth Schedules.
concepts.idea: The twelve Schedules list states, salaries, oaths, seats, areas, powers, languages, protected laws, defection and local bodies.
concepts.rule: First: names of states and union territories (Articles 1 and 4). Second: emoluments of the President, Governors, Speakers, Chairmen, judges and CAG. Third: forms of oaths or affirmations. Fourth: allocation of Rajya Sabha seats to states and union territories (Articles 4 and 80). Fifth: administration of scheduled areas and scheduled tribes (Article 244). Sixth: administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram (Articles 244 and 275). Seventh: division of powers into Union List (98 subjects, originally 97), State List (59, originally 66) and Concurrent List (52, originally 47) (Article 246). Eighth: 22 languages (originally 14); Sindhi added in 1967, Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali in 1992, Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali in 2003, Oriya renamed Odia in 2011. Ninth: Acts and regulations (originally 13, now 282) dealing with land reforms, added by the 1st Amendment (1951) to protect laws from review; laws added after 24 April 1973 are open to judicial review (Article 31B). Tenth: disqualification on ground of defection, added by the 52nd Amendment (1985). Eleventh: powers of Panchayats, 29 matters, 73rd Amendment (Article 243G). Twelfth: powers of Municipalities, 18 matters, 74th Amendment (Article 243W).
concepts.example: The Tenth Schedule contains the anti-defection law.

concepts.name: Table 4.4: sources of the Constitution
concepts.description: The countries and Acts and the features borrowed from each.
concepts.idea: Table 4.4 lists nine sources and the features borrowed from each.
concepts.rule: 1. Government of India Act 1935: federal scheme, office of Governor, judiciary, public service commissions, emergency provisions, advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and administrative details. 2. British Constitution: parliamentary government, rule of law, legislative procedure, single citizenship, cabinet system, prerogative writs, parliamentary privileges and bicameralism. 3. US Constitution: fundamental rights, independence of the judiciary, judicial review, impeachment of the President, removal of Supreme Court and High Court judges and the post of Vice-President. 4. Irish Constitution: Directive Principles, nomination of members to the Rajya Sabha and method of election of the President. 5. Canadian Constitution: a federation with a strong Centre, residuary powers with the Centre and appointment of state Governors by the Centre. 6. Australian Constitution: Concurrent List, freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse, and joint sitting of the two Houses. 7. Weimar Constitution of Germany: suspension of Fundamental Rights during emergency. 8. Soviet Constitution: Fundamental Duties and the ideal of justice in the Preamble. 9. French Constitution: the Republic and the ideals of liberty, equality and fraternity. Also South Africa (procedure for amendment and election of Rajya Sabha members) and Japan (procedure established by law).
concepts.example: The Concurrent List was borrowed from Australia.
